title: Schema Oracle and Parameter Diagnostics for Tool Calls
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: runtime and SDKs surface opaque error blobs when a model emits a tool/function call JSON that doesn't match an API contract. This causes developer confusion and costly iterations when onboarding new tool manifests or evolving parameters.

Goal: define a compact, runtime-friendly 'schema oracle' and a diagnostic envelope that bridges authoring-time JSON schema (authoritative source) and the runtime's tolerant validation/coercion behavior. Produce human-friendly error messages, actionable repair hints, and machine-friendly error codes for automatic remediations (SDK-level coercion, suggested fallback call).

Proposed solution (high level):
- Authoring format: adopt a constrained JSON-schema-lite manifest (subset of Draft 7 semantics) with added runtimeHints and recoveryHints fields. The manifest remains a single JSON document per tool/function.
- Validator behavior: runtime performs two phases: 1) strict check for required/shape violations to decide whether to reject the call; 2) permissive pass that attempts coercions (string->number, pluralization, simple enums) if policy allows. Both phases generate diagnostics.
- Diagnostic envelope: standardized fields: error_code, human_message, field_path, raw_error, suggested_fix, severity, can_auto_coerce, telemetry_hint. Example codes: E_PARAM_MISSING, E_TYPE_MISMATCH, E_ENUM_VIOLATION, E_EXTRANEOUS_FIELD, E_COERCION_FAILED.
- Authoring UX: Console lint rules surface diagnostics pre-deploy and offer quick-fix suggestions (auto-add required flags, example values).
- Compatibility: schema oracle supports a versioned compatibility policy (strict, compat, forgiving). Newer versions may mark fields deprecated with a removal_date and migration_hint.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full JSON Schema vs subset: full schema is expressive but increases runtime parsing cost and developer cognitive load. We opt for a limited subset with extensibility points.
- Strict reject-first vs permissive-first: choose reject-first for safety by default, allow project-level policy to enable permissive/coercion modes for rapid iteration.

Acceptance criteria (see separate field) and rollout plan included below.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts a tool manifest in the new manifest format and validates at startup without significant latency regression (<=3% CPU).
When a call fails validation, runtime emits a diagnostic envelope with error_code, field_path, human_message and suggested_fix.
SDK surfaces the top-1 human_message and provides an opt-in auto-coercion path when can_auto_coerce is true.
Console lint shows the same diagnostic messages during manifest authoring and links to suggested fixes.
Telemetry emits one diagnostic event per failed call containing schema_version, error_code, and route metadata for aggregation.

comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Kapoor: Triage - scoped this as a cross-team effort between runtime, SDK, and Console. Initial spike agreed.

2025-02-18 Marco Li: Spike complete - implemented a small validator that supports types: string, number, boolean, object, array, enum and added runtimeHints for coercion. Observed ~1.8% CPU overhead in our microbench. Putting proposal for review.
2025-02-20 Design (Lena Ortiz): Reviewed quick-fix flows. Asked for clearer messaging for deprecated fields and a migration_hint in suggested_fix. Added to spec.
2025-02-24 Security (Omar Hassan): Flagged that telemetry must not include raw user payloads. Updated telemetry_hint to only contain schema id and error codes. Implemented scrub rule in prototype.

2025-02-27 QA (Priya Menon): Found a regression when coercing arrays of numbers from comma-separated strings; added a test and a fallback to treat single-value strings as single-element arrays if policy = compat. Added to tasks.
2025-03-01 Marco Li: PR #4021 opened for runtime prototype; requesting eng review and perf baseline run against staging traces. Next: SDK changes and console lint integration.
